name: Al Qurna

queries.query: Al Qurna Iraq cadastral map parcel official GIS land registry
queries.result: Official-source discovery found the Iraqi Ministry of Justice real-estate-registration directory, which lists the Directorate of Real Estate Registration in Al Qurna, and the official Ur deed/map service. The service page states that electronic availability is currently limited to Baghdad and is planned for expansion; no public parcel viewer or anonymous parcel-vector endpoint was exposed.

queries.query: العراق القرنة خارطة عقارية كادستر تسجيل عقاري رسمي
queries.result: البحث في المصادر الرسمية وجد مديرية تسجيل عقاري القرنة ضمن دليل وزارة العدل، كما وجد خدمة طلب سند وخارطة العقار عبر بوابة أور. صفحة الخدمة تقصر الإتاحة الإلكترونية الحالية على بغداد، ولم يظهر عارض خرائط عقارية عام أو استجابة مجهولة تجمع هوية عقار وهندسته.

registryEvidence.custodian: The Iraqi Ministry of Justice, General Directorate of Real Estate Registration, is the national custodian; its official contact directory specifically lists the Directorate of Real Estate Registration in Al Qurna. Ministry reporting also describes work at the Basra, Basra 2, Al Qurna, and Al Madina directorates.
registryEvidence.scope: This is direct evidence of a local cadastral/real-estate-registration custodian, not evidence of public parcel-vector access. The official Ur deed/map procedure is a transaction/service workflow and not an anonymous map API.

parcelDiscovery.source: Official Ministry of Justice and Ur service routes were checked. No safe anonymous parcel ID-plus-geometry response or public map configuration was returned.

attemptedRoutes.outcome: HTTP 200 official Ministry of Justice contact directory; it lists مديرية تسجيل عقاري القرنة (Directorate of Real Estate Registration in Al Qurna). No parcel geometry, viewer, schema, or API endpoint was present.

HTTP 200 official Ministry article reporting inspection of the Basra 1, Basra 2, Al Qurna, and Al Madina registration directorates. It confirms institutional scope but provides no public parcel-vector service or geometry.

HTTP 200 official Ur service page for requesting a deed and property map. The page says electronic availability is currently in Baghdad and will expand to other directorates; it is a service workflow requiring owner/agent identity checks, not an anonymous parcel API. No login, credentials, CAPTCHA, private token, or unsafe field request was attempted.

Official electronic service entrypoint reviewed via public search result; it describes the same deed/map request and Baghdad-only current availability. No public map viewer, JavaScript parcel configuration, schema, CRS, or bounded parcel response was exposed.

Official Ur land-form complaint entrypoint reviewed only as a public route. It is a Baghdad/Dawra complaint form with unsafe property/owner fields and is not a parcel viewer; no parcel query was submitted.

parcelDiscovery.note: The exact WUP point was preserved and was not shifted or used as an absence test. No exact-point parcel query was issued because no public parcel layer was exposed. A map extent miss, login/service limitation, or absent geometry response is not evidence of citywide absence.

uncertainty: A local Al Qurna real-estate-registration directorate is directly evidenced, but its parcel database, map viewer, and machine-readable geometry access are not public through the routes reviewed.
The Ur deed/map workflow may support authorized transactions or future directorate expansion, but no authenticated or owner-specific route was used.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, personal, tax, account, certificate, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.
No sample GeoJSON was written because no safe native parcel identity plus full polygon was returned.
Packet completion is not source integration or runtime admission.
